raw_response:
I am a 62-year-old farmer with primary schooling, farming 2.2 mu in Quzhou County. I have been doing this for forty years, and my land is all I have. My wife and I are the only ones at home now — our children work in Handan and send a little money, but I do not rely on that for the farm. This field has fed my family for generations, and I know every corner of it.

It is early October, and I need to get the winter wheat in the ground soon. I saved most of the seed from last year’s harvest, but I will buy a small bag of new seed from the county store to mix in. The old seed is fine, but if you use only saved seed year after year, the wheat gets weak and the yield drops. I cannot afford all new seed — that would be over 50 yuan per mu, and on 2.2 mu that adds up fast. Mixing saved and new costs me about 10 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, I know the soil is getting tired. Last year I put down a bit less because fertilizer prices went up, and I could see the wheat was not as strong. This year I will spread about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that is roughly one big bag for the whole plot. I work it in with the rotary tiller, then broadcast the seed by hand and drag a plank to cover it. At jointing time in March, if the wheat looks yellow, I will topdress with about 8 kg of urea per mu. I would like to do more, but urea is expensive and electricity for irrigation costs money too. I have to leave some cash for the maize season.

Irrigation is a hard choice. The well is there, but the pump runs on electricity and every time I water it hurts. For wheat, I will irrigate twice — once after planting if it stays dry, and again at jointing in spring. Wheat is our main food, so I cannot take risks with it. For the summer maize, I will probably irrigate once after planting if the June rain does not come. The summer rains usually help, and maize is tougher than wheat.

Pesticide — I will spray herbicide once for each crop. I do not like spending on chemicals, but if the weeds get ahead of you, you lose more than the spray costs. I do not bother with insecticide unless I see something eating the plants. Last year there were some aphids on the maize, but not enough to matter.

The maize goes in the day after we harvest the wheat in early June. There is almost no time — sometimes only two or three days between crops. I do not do much tillage for maize; just a quick pass with the rotary tiller if the ground is hard, then plant with the hand planter. All the fertilizer for maize goes in the furrow at planting — about 18 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. There is no time for split application, and anyway I am too busy in June.

Labor is just my wife and me. We do everything ourselves. Hiring labor costs at least 150 yuan a day now, maybe more at harvest time. On 2.2 mu, there is simply no money for that. The wheat takes us about 7 family days over the season, and the maize about 6. My back is not what it used to be at sixty-two, but we manage.

I expect about 370 kg per mu of wheat and 410 kg per mu of maize if the weather is normal. Last year was decent, not great. I do not expect miracles — I just need enough grain for our own food and a little to sell for cash. My total spending on inputs this year will be about 470 yuan. That is a lot for us, but if I do not spend it, I will get nothing back.
